GrafanaRuleListItem no longer receives a ruler rule, but AlertRuleMenu still renders MenuItemPauseRule only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`. Users who are allowed to pause (prom-based `canPause` is true) lose the Pause/Resume action in the list view, which is a regression from the previous ruler-backed rendering. Make the pause menu item work from the GrafanaPromRuleDTO (uid + isPaused) when no ruler rule is available.

`canDelete` now includes the prom-based ability, but the Delete item is still rendered only when `canDelete && rulerRule`, and `rulerRule` is always undefined in the list view after this PR. Users with delete permission can no longer delete rules from the list (the new test even expects only 4 items). Change the delete handler to accept the rule identifier so it can run without a RulerRuleDTO.

The `key={key}` prop was dropped when GrafanaRuleListItem replaced GrafanaRuleLoader inside `rules.map`, while the datasource and unknown branches still pass a key. React falls back to index-based reconciliation, which logs key warnings and can attach component state (e.g. open menus, silence/delete modals) to the wrong rule as the infinite-scroll list grows. Add `key={key}` to GrafanaRuleListItem.

useAllAlertRuleAbilities used to treat federated rule groups as immutable via isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group). It now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hard-codes `isFederated = false`. As a result, Update, Delete and Pause on federated Mimir rule groups in the CombinedRule-based views are now reported as supported. Fix: keep the federated check in useAllAlertRuleAbilities, for example by passing an `isFederated` flag computed from rule.group into the shared implementation.

When useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gets skipToken (rule undefined), loading is false, so MaybeSupported is AlwaysSupported and Duplicate becomes `toAbility(AlwaysSupported, grafana create permission)`. AlertRuleMenu ORs this into canDuplicate for every non-Grafana (data-source) rule, so Duplicate is enabled whenever the user can create Grafana rules, even if the ruler ability says no. Fix: when `rule` is undefined, return NotSupported for every ability (for example `const MaybeSupported = !rule || loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`).

issues.descricao: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.

comentarios.texto: The new Prometheus-based pause ability cannot display Pause or Resume for list-view rules because the menu still requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) before rendering MenuItemPauseRule. GrafanaRuleListItem now supplies only promRule, so these actions disappear even for editable rules. Adapt the pause menu item to accept the Grafana identifier and Prometheus pause state, or load the ruler rule on demand.

issues.descricao: The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

comentarios.texto: The new Prometheus-based delete ability is still gated by `canDelete && rulerRule` when rendering the Delete item. Both Grafana list-view paths now omit rulerRule, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action entirely. Render deletion using the available identifier and group identifier instead of requiring the ruler DTO, adapting the callback contract accordingly.

issues.descricao: When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: canDuplicate ORs ruler ability with grafana ability where grafana path is skipToken=>undefined for cloud rules, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) returns Duplicate=[true,true] whenever the user has global Grafana create permission. WHY: Any user with Grafana rule-create gets Duplicate menu item on cloud/Mimir rules even when ruler abilities deny it — incorrect authorization gating. HOW: Return NotSupported for all abilities when rule is skipToken/undefined, or gate grafana branch on prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) before ORing.

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities returns AlwaysSupported for Duplicate when rule is undefined (skipToken): loading is false from the !rule early-return, so MaybeSupported=true and duplicateSupported=true. ORed in AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons this leaks Grafana create permission into non-Grafana rules. Gate MaybeSupported/duplicateSupported on rule existence (e.g. NotSupported when !rule).

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities must return NotSupported for all actions when rule is undefined (skipToken). Currently MaybeSupported falls back to AlwaysSupported when !loading, so Duplicate=[true, global-create] is true for a cloud rule passed as skipToken, and AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons OR-logic then incorrectly enables Duplicate (and Explore). Guard with if (!rule) return all-NotSupported abilities or make MaybeSupported require rule.

issues.descricao: The refactor of useAllAlertRuleAbilities into useAllRulerRuleAbilities drops the isFederatedRuleGroup check (isFederated is hardcoded false), so federated Mimir rules are reported as editable and deletable.

comentarios.texto: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated = false. The previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check is gone, so federated Mimir rules are no longer treated as immutable and can show edit and delete abilities. Keep the federation check in this wrapper, or pass the federation state into the shared hook.

Delegating useAllAlertRuleAbilities to useAllRulerRuleAbilities discards the group's federation status and replaces the previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check with a constant false. Legacy RuleActionsButtons consequently enables editing rules in groups with source_tenants, although these groups were explicitly immutable before this change. Preserve the CombinedRule federation check in the wrapper or pass federation status into the delegated ability calculation.

Preserve the federated-group immutability check when delegating this CombinedRule hook. Previously useAllAlertRuleAbilities inspected rule.group with isFederatedRuleGroup and disabled modification/removal for federated rules. The replacement delegates to a hook that hardcodes isFederated=false and receives no group information. Existing useAlertRuleAbility/useAlertRuleAbilities consumers therefore now receive supported update/delete abilities for federated rules when datasource permissions allow them, exposing operations that the previous contract explicitly prohibited. Pass the federation state through or retain that restriction in this wrapper.

issues.descricao: The Grafana prom-rule abilities gate Pause, Restore, Export and DeletePermanently on alertingRule(rule) while the comment claims it checks Grafana-managed rules, so Grafana recording rules lose these actions in the list view.

comentarios.texto: The comment says all GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed, but the variable it describes is `isAlertingRule`. That variable is true only for alerting rules and false for Grafana recording rules. Fix the comment, or rename the variable, so it says the check is for alerting rules. As written, readers will expect Pause, Export and Silence to be enabled for recording rules.

The comment says all GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed, but the check used is alertingRule(rule), which is false for recording rules. Pause, Restore, ModifyExport and DeletePermanently are therefore wrongly disabled for Grafana recording rules, where the old isGrafanaManagedAlertRule check allowed them. Use prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule) for these abilities, and keep alertingRule only for Silence.

WHAT: Grafana branch of FilterViewResults renders GrafanaRuleListItem without key={key} while datasource and unknown branches pass key. HOW: use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

The two files must agree; should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)).

issues.descricao: The comment describing the topic-list cell default color still names a plain scale-color($primary, 50%) rule that the PR replaced with dark-light-choose.

comentarios.texto: The comment at lines 72-74 states "the default for table cells in topic list is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)", but the rule it documents was converted by this PR to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100-X%))` (here for coldmap-high/med/low and in common/base/_topic-list.scss th/td). The prose still names a single `$primary` expression, so it no longer describes the code: a reader comparing the two will look for a plain `$primary` 50% rule that no longer exists. Update the comment to describe the dark-light-choose baseline (e.g. "is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))").

issues.descricao: In dark themes the notification badge background becomes a lightened $secondary while its text stays $secondary, giving dark text on a dark background with poor contrast.

comentarios.texto: The dark-theme notification badge background now uses a lightened $secondary while its text still uses the unmodified $secondary. This puts dark text on a dark background for plain badges such as category unread counts in site-map.hbs:73; with $secondary black, the foreground is #000 and the background is approximately #4d4d4d (about 2.5:1 contrast), making the small count text difficult to read. Set the default badge foreground, including its &[href] rule, to a contrasting dark-theme color such as $primary when selecting this dark background.

sugestoes.texto: The OAuth `state` is set to `pipeline.signature`, which is an md5 of the pipeline view class names (pipeline/base.py:133). That value is identical for every user and session, as the tests show with the hardcoded `9cae5e88…`. An attacker can therefore build a valid callback URL with their own GitHub `code` and send it to a victim, so the victim's pipeline binds the attacker's GitHub login (OAuth login CSRF). Generate a random per-pipeline nonce (e.g. `secrets.token_hex`), store it with `pipeline.bind_state`, and compare it against `fetch_state` with `constant_time_compare`.

When no `Integration` row exists yet for the `installation_id` supplied in the request, the view calls `pipeline.next_step()` without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to the user who installed the app. Anyone who reaches setup with another account's `installation_id` before the installation webhook creates the row skips the new user check entirely. In this branch, fetch the installation from the GitHub API (or wait for or require the webhook data) and check its installer against `github_authenticated_user` before continuing.

`integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is read without a guard, but `build_integration` only sets `sender` when it is present in state (line 376). Older or pipeline-created integrations may have no `sender`, so this raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the error page. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and call `error()` when it is missing.

`safe_urlopen` sits outside the try block, and `get_user_info` calls `resp.raise_for_status()` with no handler. Network failures or 4xx/5xx responses from GitHub (for example an expired or revoked token) therefore raise unhandled exceptions and return a 500 instead of the installation error page. Wrap the token exchange and the `get_user_info` call in try/except and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure.

issues.descricao: error() calls _(error_short) on a variable and callers pass plain literals, so the short error strings are no longer extractable for translation.

comentarios.texto: The helper calls `_(error_short)` on a variable, and callers pass plain string literals. The translation extractor cannot see these strings, so the short error messages sent to the user are no longer translatable; the old code wrapped the literals directly in `_()`. Mark the literals with gettext_lazy at the call sites and the default, and pass them through without wrapping again.

error_short strings bypass translation extraction: _(error_short) uses a variable so makemessages cannot collect them. Wrap literals at definition/call sites, e.g. error_short=_("Invalid installation request.") and pass _("...") literals, then use data error value directly without re-wrapping.

Translate the short-message literals at their definition/call sites instead of calling `_(error_short)` on a variable. Django's message extraction cannot extract the default `"Invalid installation request."` or the plain-string arguments at the two call sites from this dynamic gettext invocation. The existing pending-deletion and already-installed messages previously appeared directly inside `_()`; this refactor removes their extraction sites, and the new default message cannot enter translation catalogs. Use a translated default and translated arguments, then place `error_short` directly into the payload so these user-facing errors remain localizable.

issues.descricao: The org parameter of error()/get_document_origin is actually the active-organization context, not an Organization, so the name is misleading.

comentarios.texto: The parameter is named `org` but the code treats it as the pipeline's active-organization context: it dereferences `org.organization` and every caller (error() and the GitHubInstallation sites) passes `self.active_organization`, not an Organization. The name misstates the argument's type/contract — a caller following the name and passing a real Organization would hit AttributeError on `.organization`. Rename the parameter (e.g. `active_organization`) and correct the corresponding name in `error()` at line 131 so the two signatures match what is actually passed.

issues.descricao: The GitHub OAuth state is pipeline.signature, a static md5 of the pipeline view names, instead of a per-attempt random nonce, so it gives no CSRF protection.
issues.textoGolden: OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

comentarios.texto: The OAuth state is pipeline.signature, which Pipeline.__init__ computes solely from pipeline view class names and therefore shares across all users and installation attempts. An attacker can obtain an OAuth code for their own GitHub account and send a callback using this known state to a victim with an active installation pipeline, binding the attacker's GitHub identity to the victim's flow instead of rejecting the forged callback. Generate a random per-attempt nonce, store it in pipeline state, and validate that nonce on the OAuth callback.

Do not use pipeline.signature as OAuth state. It is a deterministic MD5 of the pipeline identifiers, not an unpredictable nonce tied to this user's authorization attempt (the tests reuse it across users). An attacker can know the expected state and submit a callback containing a code authorized under the attacker's GitHub account, defeating the OAuth login-CSRF protection and the intended binding to the installing user. Generate a cryptographically random per-attempt state, store it in the session/pipeline, and validate and consume it on callback.

issues.descricao: The new OAuth step's token exchange and user lookup are not wrapped in error handling, so GitHub/network failures surface as 500s instead of the installation-failed page.

comentarios.texto: The token request is executed outside the try block. If GitHub's token endpoint is unavailable or the request fails with a connection/timeout error, safe_urlopen raises before the guarded response parsing is reached, and this new installation step returns an unhandled server error instead of the installation-failed response. Include the request itself in the error handling and handle the relevant transport exceptions.

WHAT: safe_urlopen token exchange and get_user_info() (which calls resp.raise_for_status()) are called with no exception handling. WHY: Any network error, timeout, or non-2xx from GitHub bubbles up as an unhandled exception and 500s the install instead of rendering the invalid-request page. HOW: Wrap the exchange plus get_user_info in try/except and return error() on failure.

safe_urlopen() and get_user_info() are called outside any try/except, so network errors, non-2xx responses, or API failures raise unhandled exceptions instead of returning error(). Wrap the token exchange + user-info fetch in try/except and return error() on failure, matching the handled missing-access_token path.

issues.descricao: When no Integration exists yet for the installation_id the pipeline advances without comparing the OAuth user to the installer, bypassing the new ownership check.

comentarios.texto: The missing Integration branch advances the pipeline without verifying that github_authenticated_user installed the supplied installation_id. When the installation webhook has not created a record, or the local record was deleted, finish_pipeline calls build_integration using app credentials and attaches the installation without checking the OAuth user's access, allowing a user with another account's installation ID to bypass the new ownership check. Fail closed until trusted installer information is available and apply the ownership check before every successful next_step.

The record-absent path advances the pipeline before checking whether the authenticated GitHub user installed this app. Installation IDs arrive from the request, and a missing Integration record (for example before the installation webhook is processed) does not establish ownership. As a result, this path can attach an installation belonging to a different GitHub user despite the new authenticity check. Verify the authenticated user's authorization for the installation before advancing in this branch too, rather than relying on the webhook-created record existing.

When no Integration row exists for the installation_id, the code calls next_step() without comparing the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user to the installer. An attacker can supply an installation_id they do not own before the installation webhook has created the row, and bypass the new verification. Do not skip the check in this branch. Either fail closed, or verify ownership another way, for example by confirming the user can access the installation through the GitHub API.

issues.descricao: The installer check indexes integration.metadata['sender']['login'] without checking that sender exists, raising KeyError for integrations created without sender metadata.
issues.textoGolden: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation

comentarios.texto: integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] is indexed without checking that "sender" exists, so an ACTIVE integration whose metadata has no sender raises KeyError (500) here. metadata["sender"] is only populated when state.get("sender") is set (integration.py:376-377), and the only writer of that state is the installation webhook (webhook.py:202-208); integrations created through the pipeline itself carry no sender (confirmed by installation.py:44 which explicitly guards `if "sender" not in integration.metadata`, and by the pipeline-created integration in test_integration.py:730-743). Previously this branch only bound state and called pipeline.next_step(), so this crash is newly introduced. Fix: guard the lookup, e.g. `if pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != (integration.metadata.get("sender") or {}).get("login"):` and decide the desired fallback when sender is absent.

`integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` can raise KeyError. build_integration (line 376-377) only sets metadata["sender"] when state.get("sender") is truthy, so an existing Integration without a sender entry makes this subscripting throw an unhandled KeyError (500) instead of routing to the intended error page. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` (and treat a missing sender as a failed verification) so the mismatch/absence case returns error() rather than crashing.

The new ownership check indexes integration.metadata['sender']['login'] even though GitHubIntegrationProvider.build_integration omits sender for normal pipeline-created integrations. Reconnecting an existing active integration without an OrganizationIntegration and without webhook-populated sender now raises KeyError and returns a server error rather than an installation failure. Handle missing sender explicitly and return the invalid-installation response when trusted installer metadata is unavailable.

issues.descricao: test_installation_not_found uses a wrong OAuth state, so it fails at the state check and never reaches the installation-not-found path it is meant to test.

comentarios.texto: First response (installation_id) is overwritten by second response (bad state) with no assertion, so the Integration.DoesNotExist / not-ACTIVE branch in GitHubInstallation is never verified. Keep/assert the first flow through a valid OAuth step to reach the installation check instead of only asserting the OAuth state-mismatch error.

This test no longer verifies the "installation not found" path it exists for. The second GET supplies state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, which is not the github pipeline signature (that is the 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3 asserted in test_github_setup and reused elsewhere). OAuthLoginView.dispatch (integration.py:412-413) therefore returns error() before GitHubInstallation runs, producing the same generic "Invalid installation request." message and the same failed template via the state-mismatch branch. The Integration.DoesNotExist handling at integration.py:493-498 is never reached, so the test would still pass if that handling were removed or broken. Use the real pipeline state so the request advances into GitHubInstallation, or assert on something that distinguishes the state-mismatch branch from the missing-installation branch.

The replacement assertion no longer verifies that a nonexistent installation is rejected: 'Invalid installation request.' is also returned for a state mismatch, missing access token, or missing authenticated login before GitHubInstallation is reached. This test can therefore pass with installation-not-found handling broken if the callback fails OAuth validation instead. Establish a successful OAuth exchange with the actual pipeline state and verify that the nonexistent installation lookup is reached and rejected, rather than accepting this shared authentication-error message alone.

sugestoes.texto: TagDevice now returns ErrDeviceLimitReached to make Authenticate reject the request, but tagDeviceUI has already written the device's cache key (localCache.SetDefault at line 87) before CreateOrUpdateDevice fails. The next request from the same device gets a cache hit, tagDeviceUI returns nil, and anonymous authentication succeeds, so a device over the limit only fails once and then gets in for 29 minutes. Remove the cache entry when CreateOrUpdateDevice fails, or only set it after a successful write.

updateDevice treats rowsAffected==0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL, RowsAffected counts only rows whose values actually changed. If a known device sends another request with the same IP and user agent within the same second (updated_at has second precision), 0 rows are reported and the device is wrongly denied. Check whether the device exists with a SELECT (or use a found-rows client flag) instead of relying on the affected-row count.

The device limit is checked with a separate COUNT query and then the upsert runs, with no transaction or lock between them. Concurrent first-time requests from different devices can all see count < deviceLimit and all insert, so the configured limit is exceeded. Do the count and insert atomically, for example inside one transaction with proper locking, or as a conditional INSERT ... SELECT that checks the count.

ProvideAnonDBStore now takes a `deviceLimit int64` parameter, but it is still registered as a provider in pkg/server/wire.go:374 (bound to anonstore.AnonStore), and nothing in the dependency graph provides an int64. Wire code generation will fail, or it will inject a separate store that ignores the configured limit. Remove ProvideAnonDBStore and the AnonStore binding from wire.go, or change the provider to read the limit from *setting.Cfg.

Anonymous authentication is now denied once the device count reaches the limit, and devices are keyed by the client-supplied X-Grafana-Device-Id header with no validation. One unauthenticated client can send requests with many random device IDs to fill the limit, which locks every legitimate new anonymous visitor out for the 30-day expiration window (denial of service). Tie device identity to something the server controls, or rate-limit new device registration per IP before enforcing the limit.

Device tagging used to run in a background goroutine with its own timeout and now runs synchronously inside every anonymous Authenticate call. When device_limit is set, each uncached device runs a COUNT(*) over anon_device for the 30-day window plus an upsert while the request waits. This adds DB round-trips and count-scan latency to the anonymous auth path, which gets worse as traffic and table size grow. Keep the non-limit work asynchronous, or cache the device count (for example refresh it periodically) instead of counting on every new device.

The WithDbSession callback reassigns the captured `args` with `args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)`, and WithDbSession retries this callback on SQLite lock errors (sqlstore/session.go retryOnLocks), so each retry adds the query string to the front again. On retry, Exec gets the query string as an extra bind argument and the real values shift by one position, so the UPDATE fails or binds the wrong values whenever a lock retry happens. Build the argument list in a local variable inside the closure (e.g. `execArgs := append([]interface{}{query}, args...)`) and leave the captured slice unchanged.

issues.descricao: The device limit check counts devices and then inserts in separate non-atomic steps, so concurrent requests from new devices can all pass the check and exceed the configured limit.
issues.textoGolden: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

comentarios.texto: The limit check counts devices and then inserts in separate steps with no lock or transaction. Concurrent requests from new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the limit is exceeded. Make the count-and-insert atomic, for example with a conditional INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < limit.

The device limit check is a non-atomic count followed by an insert. Concurrent requests from different new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the number of devices exceeds deviceLimit. Make the check and insert atomic, for example with a conditional INSERT ... SELECT WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < limit, or serialize the check and insert under a lock.

WHAT: CreateOrUpdateDevice does check-then-act (CountDevices then INSERT/UPSERT) with no lock, transaction, or unique-guard when deviceLimit>0. WHY: Two concurrent new-device requests can both observe count < limit and both insert, exceeding the configured limit and breaking the enforcement contract. HOW: Enforce atomically (e.g., conditional insert guarded by count in one statement/transaction with serializable lock, or re-check count on conflict).

issues.descricao: Device slots are keyed by the client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header with no validation or rate limiting, so an anonymous caller can fill the limit with fake IDs and deny anonymous access to every new legitimate device.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Device slots counted toward deviceLimit are keyed by the unauthenticated X-Grafana-Device-Id header (read in impl.go TagDevice) with no validation or rate-limit. WHY: Any anonymous caller can mint arbitrary device IDs to fill the table up to the limit, after which all legitimate new anonymous devices get ErrDeviceLimitReached and authentication is denied — a trivial anonymous-access DoS introduced by the limit. HOW: Do not let a single client consume many slots (e.g., bind slot consumption to IP/fingerprint, rate-limit new-device creation, or require proof of distinct device).

issues.descricao: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected at the limit and never verifies that an existing device can still be updated at the limit.

comentarios.texto: The at-limit call reuses a brand-new device ID ("keep") that was never inserted, so it only reaches updateDevice's `rowsAffected == 0` -> ErrDeviceLimitReached branch. The success branch of the newly added updateDevice (an existing device still being updated while the store is at the limit) is never exercised by any test — every other call uses deviceLimit 0, so updateDevice is never invoked. A regression that made updateDevice always affect 0 rows, use a wrong WHERE/SET, or unconditionally return ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever limit>0 would leave this and all other tests green. Add a case that, after the store is at the limit, calls CreateOrUpdateDevice again with the SAME DeviceID and asserts require.NoError (and ideally that client_ip/user_agent/updated_at were changed), so the update path is actually verified.

TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected at the limit. It would still pass if updateDevice always returned ErrDeviceLimitReached, because it never re-submits the existing device (DeviceID "32mdo31deeqwes") at the limit. Add a call that updates the existing device with a new UserAgent or UpdatedAt, require NoError, and check the stored row changed.

issues.descricao: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
issues.textoGolden: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TagDevice failures that triggered the new ErrDeviceLimitReached early-return are not permanent, because tagDeviceUI (impl.go:87) writes the device key into localCache BEFORE CreateOrUpdateDevice (impl.go:93) and never evicts it on error; tagDeviceUI returns early on any cache hit (impl.go:83-84). WHY: the first request from a new over-limit device is denied, but the poisoned cache makes every subsequent request from that same device skip the limit check entirely and authenticate successfully, so the configurable device limit is bypassed by simply retrying. HOW: only set the cache key after CreateOrUpdateDevice returns nil (e.g. move a.localCache.SetDefault after the successful DB write, or delete the key when it returns ErrDeviceLimitReached).

TagDevice now propagates ErrDeviceLimitReached to deny an over-limit anonymous device, but tagDeviceUI (impl.go:83-95) records the device in localCache at line 87 *before* calling a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the store rejects the device with ErrDeviceLimitReached, the key is already cached, so the next request for that same device returns early at line 83 with a nil error and the device is admitted. The limit therefore only blocks the first request and is silently bypassed on retry. Fix by only setting the cache entry after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds (move SetDefault after the store call), or by removing/not caching the key on failure.

The new authentication gate accepts retries from devices that were rejected by the limit because tagDeviceUI inserts the cache entry before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds. At capacity, the first request with a new X-Grafana-Device-Id fails, but subsequent requests with that same ID hit the 29-minute cache and receive an anonymous identity without admission to the device store. Cache only successful admissions, and ensure concurrent requests cannot treat an in-progress admission as successful.

issues.descricao: Device tagging now runs synchronously in Authenticate, adding DB round-trips on cache-miss anonymous requests where it used to be fire-and-forget.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Anonymous.Authenticate changed from fire-and-forget goroutine TagDevice to synchronous TagDevice(ctx) that runs CountDevices + INSERT/UPDATE inline. WHY: Every cache-miss anonymous authentication now blocks on two DB round-trips in the login hot path, adding latency and DB load per request where previously auth returned immediately. HOW: Restore async tagging for the non-limit path or at least decouple denial from the hot path (e.g., async count with cached count, or only synchronously enforce when near limit).

issues.descricao: The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

comentarios.texto: The new device_limit setting is read without adding a corresponding key to conf/defaults.ini. applyEnvVariableOverrides only visits keys already present in the loaded INI and runs before readAuthSettings, so setting GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone is ignored and leaves the limit at zero, disabling enforcement. Add an uncommented device_limit = 0 entry under auth.anonymous in defaults.ini so the standard environment override mechanism can apply it.

issues.descricao: The anonymous device limit is enforced only through TagDevice, which returns nil when the client-controlled device ID header is missing, so requests without the header authenticate anonymously regardless of the configured limit.

The doc comment on updateDevice says it updates a device "updated between the given times", but the function takes no times, computes the 30-day window itself and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when no row matches.
updateDevice prepends the query to the captured args inside the retried DB callback, so a SQLite lock retry runs Exec with the query duplicated in the arguments and the update fails.

sugestoes.texto: _is_error_focused_query uses a raw substring check, so queries like `!event.type:error` or `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` are treated as error-only queries. In those cases discover count() is rewritten to upsampled_count() even though the results include non-error (transaction) rows, which gives wrong counts or breaks the query on sample_weight. Parse the query with the event_search parser and only return True when there is a single positive `event.type:error` filter combined with AND.

The upsampling decision is made from the outer `dataset` closure variable instead of the `scoped_dataset` that actually runs the query. In the dashboard-split path (get_event_stats_factory), _get_event_stats is called with errors or transactions as scoped_dataset while `dataset` is metrics_enhanced or discover, so errors queries are never upsampled there and the check does not match the queried dataset. Pass `scoped_dataset` to is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects.

issues.descricao: The upsampling decision is evaluated against the request's dataset instead of the scoped_dataset actually queried, so in the dashboard discover-split path (metrics dataset) error queries run against discover skip upsampling even when all projects are allowlisted.
issues.textoGolden: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.

comentarios.texto: The upsampling decision uses the closure variable `dataset` while the transformed `final_columns` are executed against `scoped_dataset`. In the dashboard-split path `_get_event_stats` is deliberately invoked with a different dataset (e.g. `_get_event_stats(discover, ...)` at lines 351, 365, 406, 423) than the request's `dataset`, so the `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` branch can be evaluated against the wrong dataset and apply/skip `sum(sample_weight)` for a dataset that was never queried. Base the decision on the dataset actually being queried (`scoped_dataset`) so the transform matches the target of the query.

issues.descricao: _is_error_focused_query uses a substring match for `event.type:error` on the request query, so negated or mixed (OR transaction) discover queries are treated as error-only and get the sample_weight sum instead of count().

comentarios.texto: `_is_error_focused_query` decides whether to apply `upsampled_count()` by doing a naive substring search for `event.type:error` in the raw request query. A query that excludes errors (e.g. `!event.type:error`) or the discover-split query `({query}) AND event.type:transaction` still contains the literal `event.type:error`, so the transform is applied to a non-error / transactions query, summing `sample_weight` where it should be a plain `count()` and producing wrong bucket values. It also ignores the actual `query` passed to `_get_event_stats`, so the decision can differ from the query that is really executed. Match on a parsed/negation-aware condition (or pass the resolved query string) instead of a raw substring test.

The substring check treats `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` as error-only queries. For allowlisted projects this rewrites count() to an aggregation over sample_weight even when the Discover query includes transactions, violating the error-only restriction and potentially failing against a transaction-backed query. Determine the event-type restriction from the parsed query rather than the presence of a substring.

Substring matching does not establish that the Discover query selects only errors. For example, `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` both return True here, causing count() to be replaced with the sample-weight aggregation for non-error or mixed results in allowlisted projects. This contradicts the error-only guard and can produce incorrect counts. Parse the query and establish an error-only restriction (including negation and Boolean structure), or conservatively skip transformation when that restriction cannot be proven.

issues.descricao: test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events cannot detect upsampling being applied to transaction queries, because the transaction has no sample_weight and upsampled_count() equals count() for it.

comentarios.texto: test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events would still pass if upsampling were wrongly applied to transaction queries. The transaction event has no sample_weight, and upsampled_count uses ifNull(sample_weight, 1), so the result is still 1 and 0. Give the transaction a non-default sample rate or weight so an upsampled count would differ from a plain count, or assert that the transform was not applied.

test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events cannot falsify over-application of upsampling: the stored transaction has no sample_weight so upsampled_count() (sum(ifNull(sample_weight,1))) returns 1, same as count(). Give the transaction a sample_weight/client_sample_rate that would diverge (e.g. count 10 if upsampled vs 1 if not), or assert via mock that transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling was not called / yAxes were not rewritten.

test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events cannot detect upsampling being wrongly applied to transaction queries. The stored transaction event has no error_sampling context, so sample_weight is null, and upsampled_count = toInt64(sum(ifNull(sample_weight,1))) evaluates to 1 for it — identical to count(). If _should_apply_sample_weight_transform/_is_error_focused_query were broken so that a discover query with event.type:transaction gets upsampled, the assertion count==1 (and 0 in the empty bucket) would still pass. Add an event with a known non-1 sample_weight (or assert the emitted query uses count() and not upsampled_count) so the test actually fails when the transaction exclusion is bypassed.

issues.descricao: The test factory helper's docstring promises a valid client sample rate but it copies any truthy float-convertible value (negative, >1, strings), unlike production validation.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling uses `if client_sample_rate: float(...)` with no type/range check, unlike production _derive_client_error_sampling_rate which requires isinstance(int,float) and 0<rate<=1. WHY: string '0.1', bool True, or out-of-range 5.0 get stored as sample_rate in fixtures while production drops them, making upsampling tests diverge from prod. HOW: mirror production validation before assigning sample_rate.

The new docstring says the client sample rate must be 'present and valid', but the implementation only checks truthiness and float conversion. Negative rates, rates greater than 1, and float-convertible non-finite values are all accepted and written to sample_rate. This falsely tells test authors that this helper enforces sample-rate validity. Either document that it merely copies truthy float-convertible values, or validate the supported sample-rate range and finiteness before setting the field.

issues.descricao: With upsampling active, top-events queries pick and order the top N groups by raw count() (selected_columns/orderby are not transformed) while the plotted series use upsampled_count(), so ranking can disagree with the displayed weighted counts.

comentarios.texto: Only timeseries_columns are upsampled while selected_columns and orderby used to select the Top N remain based on raw count(). discover.top_events_timeseries first queries those unchanged selected columns to choose groups, so a group with fewer retained events but a higher weighted count is omitted in favor of a lower-volume group. Apply the weighted-count transformation consistently to Top N selection and its ordering as well as the displayed timeseries.

issues.descricao: _are_all_projects_error_upsampled and its caller take an organization argument that is never read.

comentarios.texto: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` takes an `organization` argument — also threaded in from the public `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` — but never reads it: the body uses only `project_ids` and the global option `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`. The declared parameter is dead. Either the allowlist check is meant to be organization-scoped (the body must actually consult `organization`) or the parameter should be removed from both functions; as written the signature advertises an organization-scoped decision the implementation never makes.

issues.descricao: Claims only bare count() is rewritten, so aliased count, eps(), epm(), count_unique() etc. stay un-upsampled.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites exact bare `count()` and passes everything else through unchanged. WHY: yAxes like `count() as foo`, `eps()`, `epm()`, `count_unique()`, `count_if()` keep raw counts while should_upsample is true, returning under-counted timeseries. HOW: parse/normalize the function (strip alias, match function name with args) and rewrite all count-equivalent aggs or explicitly fall back to no-upsampling.

issues.descricao: Rewriting count() to `upsampled_count() as count` breaks responses for transformAliasToInputFormat=1: the result column is translated to the rewritten field string while the serializer still reads `count()`.

comentarios.texto: Replacing count() with `upsampled_count() as count` breaks requests using transformAliasToInputFormat=1. QueryBuilder.process_results translates the count alias to the replacement field string, but the endpoint serializer still resolves the original axis as `count()`, so it cannot read the weighted count from the returned rows. Preserve the original public field name in the result mapping when rewriting the internal aggregation.

issues.descricao: upsampled_count truncates the weighted sum with toInt64 instead of rounding, under-counting the estimate by up to one per bucket.

comentarios.texto: `upsampled_count` wraps the sum in `toInt64`, which truncates toward zero: `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))` of e.g. 1.5 or 3.33 yields 1 or 3 instead of the nearest integer, systematically under-counting the upsampled estimate (worst when weights are just below an integer). Use a rounding aggregation (e.g. `toInt64(round(sum(...)))`) so the reconstructed count reflects the intended estimate rather than a floored value.

issues.descricao: The 'no project IDs' test case runs with an empty allowlist mock, so it passes via the empty-allowlist branch and does not verify the empty project_ids guard.

comentarios.texto: The 'no project IDs provided' case does not exercise the `if not project_ids: return False` guard. mock_options.get.return_value was set to [] just above (line 48), so removing the project_ids guard still returns False via the `if not allowlist` branch, and this assertion passes either way. Re-mock options.get to return a non-empty allowlist (e.g. self.project_ids) before calling with project_ids=[], so the empty-project guard is actually falsifiable.

issues.descricao: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` checks membership against the allowlist list for each project; converting it to a set would avoid O(N*M) lookups.

sugestoes.texto: The fail-fast check for multiple providers was removed, but DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider and WildFlyElytronProvider all return order() 200, so the stable sort keeps them in ServiceLoader order and get(0) picks one of them depending on classpath order. A deployment that ends up with both the FIPS and non-FIPS providers on the classpath now starts quietly with whichever comes first, and the only trace is a debug log line, where it used to fail with an error. Fix: still throw IllegalStateException when the top two providers have the same order(), or give the FIPS, default and Elytron providers distinct order values.

For an indefinite-length byte (0x80), readLength returns -1, and readInteger then calls read(-1), which runs new byte[-1] and throws NegativeArraySizeException instead of IOException. A malformed ECDSA DER signature therefore raises an unchecked runtime exception from asn1derToConcatenatedRS, which goes against the method's IOException contract and can escape callers that only catch IOException. Fix: throw IOException("indefinite-length encoding not allowed in DER") here instead of returning -1.

issues.descricao: concatenatedRSToASN1DER encodes r and s into two throwaway ASN1Encoder instances before re-encoding them in the return statement.
issues.textoGolden: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.

comentarios.texto: Dead computation: the two ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls allocate encoders and encode rBigInteger/sBigInteger, but their results are discarded — the returned DER comes entirely from the expression at lines 117-121, which re-encodes the same BigIntegers. These two statements have no effect and should be removed (they are a leftover from an earlier formulation).

Remove these two discarded encoder writes. Each allocates an encoder and encodes a BigInteger, but neither result participates in the returned signature; lines 119–120 repeat both writes on fresh encoders. This performs redundant encoding and allocations on every concatenated-signature conversion.

The two statements `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` encode values and discard the results. The return expression re-encodes the same values, so these lines are dead computation left over from a copy-paste or refactor. Remove them.

issues.descricao: order() is added to CryptoProvider as an abstract method, breaking source and binary compatibility for existing third-party CryptoProvider implementations.
issues.textoGolden: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations

comentarios.texto: order() was added as an abstract method to the public CryptoProvider interface. CryptoIntegration.detectProvider now invokes order() on every ServiceLoader-discovered CryptoProvider via Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order). Any CryptoProvider implementation compiled against the previous interface (an external or separately built provider jar on the classpath) will throw AbstractMethodError at detection time, i.e. during AuthzClient.create()/server bootstrap, before any provider is usable. Giving order() a default implementation (e.g. default int order() { return 0; }) avoids the binary-incompatibility.

issues.descricao: detectProvider no longer fails when several crypto providers are present; with Default, FIPS and Elytron all at order 200, ties are resolved by classpath order and a FIPS deployment can silently run with the non-FIPS provider.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: detectProvider sorts by order() reversed and silently picks index 0, removing the previous multiple-providers error. WHY: Default/FIPS/Elytron all return order 200, so ambiguous classpath (e.g. default+FIPS) now nondeterministically picks one by ServiceLoader order instead of failing fast, risking wrong FIPS vs non-FIPS crypto. HOW: only auto-ignore lower-order providers; throw when the top two have equal order().

Reject ambiguous highest-priority providers rather than silently taking the first. Both DefaultCryptoProvider and FIPS1402Provider return order 200 in this PR, so when both are present the stable sort leaves the decision to ServiceLoader discovery order. A deployment expecting FIPS can therefore initialize the ordinary Bouncy Castle provider without an error; previously this mixed classpath failed closed. Preserve the error for tied highest-priority providers (or require an explicit security-mode/provider choice), while still allowing the lower-priority authz-client fallback.

detectProvider() no longer fails fast when multiple CryptoProviders are present and instead silently picks the first after sorting by order() descending. All Keycloak providers return the same order (DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider, WildFlyElytronProvider all return 200), so a tie between two providers is broken by the non-deterministic ServiceLoader iteration order rather than the intended priority. The previous code threw an IllegalStateException forcing the classpath to be corrected; now a deployment with two provider jars (exactly the 'multiple providers on classpath' scenario this PR enables) can silently select the unintended provider — e.g. a non-FIPS/strict provider when FIPS is required — with no error. Use a stable tie-breaker (delegate to the provider name/type) or reject equal top orders instead of relying on ServiceLoader order.

issues.descricao: Claims a wrong-length JOSE signature causes an unchecked exception in concatenatedRSToASN1DER; verifiers catch it and report verification failure, as with the existing providers.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: concatenatedRSToASN1DER splits signature without validating signature.length==signLength. WHY: short JOSE input throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and long input is silently truncated to signLength, breaking the ECDSACryptoProvider contract (IOException on malformed) used by verifier contexts. HOW: check length upfront and throw IOException.

concatenatedRSToASN1DER never validates signature.length == signLength before System.arraycopy(signature,0,r,1,len) / (signature,len,s,1,len). A short JWS signature throws unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of the declared IOException, breaking verification on attacker-controlled input. Validate length and throw IOException.

issues.descricao: The ES384 and ES512 tests sign with the same default P-256 key, so the converter is never tested with real P-384 or P-521 signatures.

comentarios.texto: Single default EC keypair reused for ES256/ES384/ES512: testES384/testES512 names claim larger curves but body signs with the same P-256 key and only pads to larger signLength, so full-width 384/521-bit handling is never exercised. Generate a per-algorithm keypair with the correct curve (e.g. secp256r1/secp384r1/secp521r1) before signing.

Every case generates a default EC key rather than a key on the curve associated with the named algorithm. On the standard JDK this is P-256, so testES384 and testES512 just pad P-256 signature components to larger lengths. A converter that discards nonzero high bytes beyond 32 bytes would still pass all three cases. Initialize the key generator with the appropriate curve per case (P-256, P-384, and P-521) so the larger-component conversions are actually tested.

Generate a key on the curve corresponding to each tested algorithm rather than using the provider's default EC curve for all three tests. On the standard JDK this generates a P-256 key even for testES384 and testES512, so those tests merely pad P-256 integers to larger output lengths and never exercise actual P-384/P-521 signature encoding (including P-521's long-form sequence length).

issues.descricao: The test only checks a round trip between the two new converters and never verifies the re-encoded DER against the original signature or with Signature.verify, so mutually consistent bugs go undetected.

comentarios.texto: Tautological round-trip assertion: rsConcat2 is derived from rsConcat via encode+decode that are inverses if self-consistent, so assertArrayEquals(rsConcat,rsConcat2) passes even if both directions are wrong. Verify against external oracle: Signature.initVerify + verify(asn1Des) and/or compare rsConcat to expected split, not just to itself.

The test only checks self-consistency: it asserts asn1derToConcatenatedRS(g(asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign))) == asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign), i.e. that concatenatedRSToASN1DER is a right inverse of asn1derToConcatenatedRS. It never compares against the original DER `sign`, never verifies the ECDSA signature, and never asserts the emvider output is canonical DER. Because the decoder it reads back with (ASN1Decoder.readLength) accepts non-canonical long-form lengths (e.g. 0x81) and validates only tag numbers, a regression in ASN1Encoder.writeLength that always emitted long form would still round-trip and the test would still pass, even though the produced signature would no longer be valid DER and would be rejected by the Keycloak server / a JDK Signature.verify. Assert the encoded signature is valid DER (e.g. verify it with a JDK Signature, or compare asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign) against a known-good width-padded r||s and assert its length equals algorithm.getSignatureLength()).

The assertion only establishes agreement between the two new conversion routines, not correctness of the converted signature. For example, swapping r and s in both routines makes this entire round trip pass, although the DER result no longer verifies the signed data. Verify `asn1Des` with the public key and original data (or compare against an independently specified encoding) so mutually compensating conversion defects fail the test.

issues.descricao: getBouncyCastleProvider in AuthzClientCryptoProvider returns the JDK default KeyStore provider instead of BouncyCastle, contrary to the CryptoProvider contract.
ASN1Decoder.readInteger accepts constructed INTEGER tags because it only masks the low tag bits, so malformed DER is parsed as valid.

sugestoes.texto: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which counts one page too many when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members and limit 50 gives 2 pages). The "next" button then stays enabled and leads to an empty page, and showingLast is never true on the real last page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) instead.

The public group members page now calls the paginated findMembers, which loads only the first 50 members (default limit), and group/members.hbs has no next/previous controls. For non-automatic groups the endpoint used to return everyone, so groups with more than 50 members now show a cut-off list and users have no way to see the rest. Add paging or infinite loading to the public members page.

params[:limit] comes from the client and is used with no upper bound, on a public endpoint that only requires can_see. Any caller can send limit=1000000 and have every member of a large group (e.g. trust_level_0) loaded and serialized in one request, and a negative limit raises a SQL error. Clamp the value, e.g. limit = [[params[:limit].to_i, 1].max, 200].min, and keep offset non-negative.

add_members calls group.add (users.push) for every username without skipping users who are already members, and group_users has a UNIQUE index on (group_id, user_id). If an admin adds someone who is already in the group, the insert hits the unique index and the request fails with a 500 (the old usernames= path only added the difference). Skip existing members first, e.g. `group.add(user) unless group.users.exists?(user.id)`.

remove_member deletes the membership with group.users.delete(user_id) but no longer resets the user's primary_group_id. The old destroy_deletions path did this for every removed user. A removed user keeps the group as their primary group (flair and title) even though they are no longer a member. After deleting, run `User.where(id: user_id, primary_group_id: group.id).update_all(primary_group_id: nil)`.

issues.descricao: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
issues.textoGolden: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.

comentarios.texto: totalPages (and currentPage) use `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which is an off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members, limit 50 → reports 2 pages although only 1 exists). This leaves `showingLast` false on the real last page, so 'next' navigates to an empty page at offset=user_count. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (and compute currentPage consistently) to get the correct page count.

totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives 2 for user_count=50, limit=50, although 50 members occupy exactly one page. Correct it to `Math.ceil(this.get('user_count') / this.get('limit'))`. Effect: for a group whose member count is a multiple of the page size, totalPages is one too high, showingLast remains false so the 'next' link stays enabled, and clicking it navigates to a phantom empty page.

`totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which over-counts by one whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 members with limit 50 yields 2 pages instead of 1). Since `showingLast` is `propertyEqual("currentPage", "totalPages")`, on a full last page `showingLast` is false, so the `next` action stays enabled and advances `offset` to `user_count`, rendering an empty page labeled as the last page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the zero-member guard) so the count matches the real number of pages.

issues.descricao: Several Group model functions (findMembers, destroy, userCountDisplay) return a value on some paths and undefined on others, triggering consistent-return lint warnings.
issues.textoGolden: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

issues.descricao: Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.

comentarios.texto: Guard against stale member-fetch responses before updating the model. `next` updates offset immediately and leaves navigation enabled, so with at least three pages two rapid clicks issue requests for offsets 50 and 100. If the offset-100 response arrives first and the offset-50 response arrives last, this unconditional `setProperties` resets both offset and members to the older page, undoing the latest navigation. Refreshes after membership changes can similarly be overwritten by an earlier fetch. Track a per-model request generation and apply only the latest response, or serialize navigation and refresh requests.

issues.descricao: The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.

comentarios.texto: The public members route now loads only the model's default 50-member page without providing any way to request subsequent pages. The public group/members.hbs template only renders members and has no Next/Previous controls, so members after the first 50 become inaccessible (manual groups previously returned all members). Add public pagination controls and actions that update offset and reload members.

The new default limit applies to nonautomatic groups as well, but the public group-members route still calls findMembers() only once and its template simply iterates members without pagination. Previously this endpoint returned every member of a nonautomatic group; now a group with more than 50 members exposes only the first 50 on its public members page, with no way to reach the rest. Update that consumer to fetch subsequent pages or provide pagination when introducing this endpoint contract.

Provide pagination or load subsequent pages for the public group-members view. findMembers now requests only 50 members, and this route calls it only once while its template simply iterates members without navigation. Custom groups previously returned all members, so groups larger than 50 now have members that cannot be viewed on this page.

issues.descricao: Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.

comentarios.texto: Persist params[:alias_level] when creating a group, just as update does. The creation form exposes aliasLevelOptions and group.asJSON sends the selected alias_level, but create saves only name and visible. A newly created group therefore retains the default alias level instead of the administrator's selection.

issues.descricao: Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) instead of the Group#remove destroy path. WHY: bypasses GroupUser destroy callbacks and primary_group_id cleanup done in destroy_deletions, leaving stale membership side-effects (e.g. dangling primary_group_id). HOW: load the User and call group.remove(user).

Removing a member with group.users.delete bypasses the primary_group_id cleanup previously performed by Group#destroy_deletions during usernames updates. A user whose primary group is this group remains associated with it as their primary group after membership removal, leaving stale primary-group state used by user administration and post serialization. Clear primary_group_id for the removed user when it equals this group's id as part of the removal operation.

issues.descricao: The remove_member spec issues a PUT request although the route only maps DELETE to remove_member, so the test uses a verb never routed in production.
issues.textoGolden: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

comentarios.texto: This example sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the PR maps `remove_member` only to DELETE (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`); PUT on that path routes to `groups#add_members`. Controller specs bypass the router, so the example still lands on `remove_member` and passes regardless — it would still pass if the DELETE route were missing or wired to the wrong action, leaving the newly introduced verb/action pairing untested. Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member`, as the sibling example at line 125 already does.

The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. It exercises the action with a verb that is never routed in production. Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` so the test matches the real request.

issues.descricao: Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
`add_members` runs one User query per username; load all users with a single `User.where(username: ...)` query.

sugestoes.texto: The removal listener is gated only on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, but management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on, and its clients().setPermissionsEnabled now throws UnsupportedOperationException. If both features are enabled, deleting any client (ClientRemovedEvent) throws inside the listener and the deletion transaction fails. Gate the listener on `isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) && !isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2)`, or skip the V1 setPermissionsEnabled call when V2 is active.

In V2, deleting a client no longer cleans up its per-client authorization resource (named by the client UUID in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource): setPermissionsEnabled is unsupported, and the listener in AdminPermissions is skipped when only V2 is on. The resource and the scope permissions that reference it stay in the admin-permissions client after the client is gone. Add a V2-specific handler for ClientRemovedEvent that deletes the resource found by client.getId() and updates or removes the permissions that point to it.

canView(ClientModel) chains canView(), canConfigure() and canManage(), and each step calls hasPermission. That is up to four full root.evaluatePermission runs (type VIEW, client MANAGE, client CONFIGURE, client VIEW), and every run already evaluates all scopes of the same resource before keeping only one. This happens for each client when admins list or view clients, so the policy evaluation cost per client multiplies. Evaluate the client resource once and check the returned scope set for MANAGE, CONFIGURE or VIEW, instead of calling hasPermission once per scope.

findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) also returns the schema's all-clients resource, because it is created with name and type both set to "Clients". When an all-clients permission grants the scope, the literal "Clients" is added to the result set as if it were a client id. AvailableRoleMappingResource.getRoleIdsWithPermissions then calls realm.getClientById("Clients").getRolesStream(), which throws a NullPointerException. Fix: skip the resource whose name equals CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, and if all-clients is granted, return every realm client id instead.

issues.descricao: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.
issues.textoGolden: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup is now entirely wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so when the feature is disabled the pre-existing removal cleanup (roles/clients/groups .setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)) no longer runs. Realms using the non-V2 permission model will keep orphaned authorization resources/permissions after a client, role or group is removed. The gate should preserve the old behavior when the feature is off (run for V1), or the V1 cleanup must be performed elsewhere.

issues.descricao: getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
issues.textoGolden: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

issues.descricao: Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
issues.textoGolden: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2 has an unused private getEvaluationContext method.
issues.textoGolden: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

comentarios.texto: Dead computation: `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` is private and has no caller anywhere in the class. Its only possible consumer in the V1 class, `canExchangeTo`, was overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException (line 148-150). The EvaluationContext and its overridden getBaseAttributes are built and then never used — remove the method (or wire it into canExchangeTo if token-exchange is meant to be supported).

issues.descricao: The Javadoc of the void requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() methods says they return true instead of documenting that they throw ForbiddenException.

comentarios.texto: The Javadoc for `void requireView()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}", but requireView() is void and throws ForbiddenException rather than returning a value. It is a copy-paste of the canView() doc and should read "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canView()} returns {@code false}", matching the sibling require* methods (requireListClientScopes, requireConfigure, etc.).

The Javadoc for `void requireViewClientScopes()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException. The doc describes a boolean return the method never produces; it should state that it throws ForbiddenException if canViewClientScopes() returns false, consistent with the other require* methods.

Declaration does not match the method it documents: the javadoc for `requireView()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.') and for `requireViewClientScopes()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}.') describes a boolean-returning accessor, but both methods are declared `void` and are the require* counterparts that throw ForbiddenException (as documented for requireManage/requireConfigure above). The text was copy-pasted from the corresponding can* methods; it should state that the method throws when canView()/canViewClientScopes() is false.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.

comentarios.texto: canView() does not recognize an all-clients MANAGE permission even though canView(client) grants viewing through canConfigure(client) and canManage(client). For an administrator with global MANAGE but no VIEW, ClientsResource.getClients selects an unpaginated realm-wide client stream and evaluates authorization for clients before applying pagination, instead of fetching the requested database page. Include the global MANAGE permission in the global viewing capability while preserving client-specific denial semantics.

issues.descricao: canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

comentarios.texto: The global VIEW check returns true before evaluating client-specific VIEW permissions, bypassing a negative permission on an individual client. An administrator granted VIEW on all clients can therefore read a client explicitly excluded by a client-specific denial; ClientsResource.getClients also bypasses per-client checks when this evaluator's parameterless canView() returns true. Evaluate the specific client resource before falling back to the all-clients permission, and ensure listing does not use a global grant to skip specific denials.

Do not short-circuit resource-specific view evaluation on the global fine-grained VIEW grant. With an all-clients VIEW permission allowing an administrator and a client-specific VIEW permission denying that administrator, canView() returns true here and the specific client permission is never evaluated. This differs from the specific-over-global override behavior exercised for users in this PR and exposes the denied client's representation. Keep the administrative-role bypass separate from fine-grained grants and evaluate the client's resource before falling back to the all-clients resource; also ensure the global view result used by client listing cannot bypass those overrides.

issues.descricao: The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

comentarios.texto: The expected ForbiddenException can come from getDefaultClientScopes(), before removeDefaultClientScope() is invoked. With no permission granted, the initial read is forbidden, so this test still passes if removal's manage-permission check is removed entirely; the later granted removal also succeeds in that broken implementation. Obtain the scope ID using the privileged realm client outside this try block, then invoke only removeDefaultClientScope() through the restricted client and assert that it is forbidden.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

sugestoes.texto: `include_website_name` has no trailing `?`, so ActiveModel::Serializers never calls it, and website_name is not covered by the `untrusted_attributes` restriction that hides `website` (line 109). For users where `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (e.g. TL0 users viewed by anonymous visitors), the website's host or path is still sent and displayed through website_name. Rename the method to `include_website_name?` and make it `website.present? && !scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` (or add :website_name to untrusted_attributes).

If the stored website has no scheme (e.g. 'example.com' or 'www.example.com'), `URI(website).host` is nil, so website_name returns nil. user.hbs now shows the website only `{{#if model.website_name}}`, so these profiles no longer show their website at all. Fall back to the raw website string when no host can be parsed, or parse a scheme-prefixed copy of the URL.

The 'same parent domain' check strips only the first label of each host, so on public-suffix domains it matches unrelated sites: `forum.co.uk` and `evil.co.uk` both reduce to `co.uk`. As a result, the full URL path is shown for websites that are not on the forum's domain, which is the opposite of what this feature intends. Compare registrable domains instead (for example with the public_suffix gem, or by requiring at least three labels after removing the subdomain).

issues.descricao: website_name compares hostnames case-sensitively, so an uppercase website host matching the instance domain shows only the host instead of the full path.

comentarios.texto: The new `website_name` compares two domain names case-sensitively. `URI(website.to_s).host` preserves the letter case written by the user, whereas `Discourse.current_hostname` is the canonical lower-cased host, and no side is down-cased before the comparison at lines 141, 144-146 and 149 (including the `ends_with?` suffix check). Because DNS host names are case-insensitive identity values, `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` and `http://example.com/user` denote the same host but take different branches, so the same-site check is decided by letter case: the wrong arm is chosen and the full-path form is dropped. Normalise both sides before comparing, e.g. `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host&.downcase` (or use `URI(...).hostname`, which down-cases) and compare against `Discourse.current_hostname.to_s.downcase`.

Hostname comparisons are case-sensitive even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive.
